training._iters_note: num_iterations/games_per_iteration are per variant; N=4 games run ~3x longer so it buys fewer of them for the same wall clock
training._replay_buffer_note: 100k ~= 7 iterations of coverage at N=2, the regime the 5x5 buffer ablation validated (runs/n2_5x5_buf10k_v1: 10k ~= 6 iters, identical loss_v endpoint and strength vs the 100k baseline). 500k bought nothing and cost ~1.4 GB of parent RSS.
training._ply_counted_note: max_game_moves and explore_moves both count plies, not rounds — set per variant so each player gets the same budget; see variants.n2/n4
training._discount_unit_note: Per-variant. 'round' decays gamma per the mover's own turns, 'ply' per move by anybody. Measured at 9x9: N=2 improved under round (gate 61.5%->78.8% at iter 10 vs v3), N=4 got worse (draws stalled at 46% where the ply run had reached 16%, policy loss falling instead of broadening). Round pushes the N=4 opening target to 0.71 vs 0.25 ply-counted, asserting near-certainty about a genuinely uncertain 4-player opening.
